name: How does duplex construction work on a corner lot?

mainEntity.name: What are the design and setback challenges when building a duplex on a corner lot in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What are the design and setback challenges when building a duplex on a corner lot in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Corner lots can be excellent for duplexes because they may offer more frontage, better access, and stronger curb appeal, but they also come with unique constraints. The street-side setback can be more restrictive than an interior side yard, and the building may need to respond to two public elevations instead of one. Privacy becomes a bigger issue because more windows and outdoor areas face the street and neighboring properties. Traffic, noise, and entry placement also matter more on corners. The design should solve for clear address identity, safe access, and a layout that does not feel exposed. Corner lots may also create opportunities for better light, better parking access, or a more flexible unit split if zoning allows it. The site plan should be tested carefully to make sure the building mass, garage placement, and outdoor space work together. This is one of the lot types where a custom design-build approach can save space and improve long-term livability.
acceptedAnswer.description: Corner lots often face stricter street-side setback rules, visibility concerns, and more exposure to noise and traffic. That can reduce buildable area and make privacy harder to solve, especially for windows, entries, and outdoor space. Corner-lot duplexes need site planning that balances code compliance and livability.
